sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5.93 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
The shape is a decelerating ramp: growth ran 104.0% in FY2017 and 64.2% in FY2021, then fell to 0.1% in FY2023 before recovering to 16.4% in FY2024 and 10.6% in FY2025 [D36][D218][D311][D358][D406].
FY2017's operating loss of $3.49 billion was driven by a $2.6 billion increase in stock-based compensation tied to the CEO award and IPO-related RSUs [F12][P74].
FY2022's loss widened to $1.40 billion on higher cost of revenue and operating expenses, including restructuring charges [F17][P42][P40].
The operating margin improved from -30.3% in FY2022 to -9.0% in FY2025, the window high [F27][F30][D554].
North America remains the largest geography at 58.6% of FY2025 revenue but contributed only 4.4pp of the 10.6% growth [D456][D458][D406].
Rest of world grew 17.0% and contributed 3.7pp, lifting its share to 23.0% [D498][D499][D497].
FY2025 revenue rose $570.0 million, split between a $282.4 million advertising increase on 17% more impressions and a $287.6 million other-revenue increase from subscription growth [P24].
Other revenue is now 12.6% of revenue and contributed 5.4pp of growth, nearly matching advertising's 5.3pp [D543][D545][D538].
Operating costs grew 5.1% against 10.6% revenue growth, giving an incremental operating margin of 44.8% [D423][D406][D429].
The FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% is far above the window median of -32.4% and the FY2017 low of -422.5% [F30][D555][D553].
The 5.7pp improvement in FY2025 came from cost of revenue (+1.1pp), R&D (+1.3pp) and other lines (+3.3pp) [D419][D431][D432][D433].
Sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on timing of marketing events and lower advertising spend, while R&D rose $101.9 million on product development headcount [P22][P23].
Net margin of -7.8% sits 1.2pp above operating margin, helped by $96.7 million of debt-extinguishment gains in other income [F50][D591][P18].
Against internet peers the operating margin ranks at the 0th percentile versus a 20.3% median [D570][D571].
Operating cash flow of $656.2 million exceeded the $460.5 million net loss, and free cash flow reached $437.2 million, a 7.4% margin [F80][F40][F100][D393].
Operating cash flow rose on non-cash add-backs including $1.0 billion of stock-based compensation and $163.6 million of D&A [P13].
Capex of $219.0 million was 3.7% of revenue and 1.34x D&A [F90][D392][D395].
Capex is primarily improvements to leased facilities to support team workspaces [P10].
Cash and investments of $2.94 billion against $3.54 billion of debt leaves net debt of $596.3 million, equal to 10.1% of revenue [D397][D398][D399][D400].
That net cash position ranks at the 0th percentile against internet peers, whose median is 45.0% of revenue [D578][D579].
In February 2025 the company issued $1.50 billion of 2033 Notes and repurchased $1.4 billion of 2026, 2027 and 2028 Notes [P2][P1].
Buybacks of $750.9 million were 171.7% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count still rose 2.1% [X156][D402][D425].
The company has posted a net loss in each of the last ten years, from $514.6 million in FY2016 to $460.5 million in FY2025 [R1][F31][F40].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 and has stayed above 10% for nine straight years [R2][D390].
Net cash has fallen for four consecutive years, moving from $1.44 billion in FY2021 to net debt of $596.3 million in FY2025 [R3][D211][D399].
Buybacks exceeded free cash flow in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, at 544.3%, 142.3% and 171.7% respectively [R4][D307][D354][D402].
Operating margin: a move above the FY2025 level of -9.0% would extend the four-year improvement, while a slip back toward the -32.4% median would reverse it [F30][D555].
Net cash: a return above zero would reverse the four-year slide from $1.44 billion in FY2021 to -$596.3 million in FY2025 [D211][D399].
Free cash flow margin: holding above the FY2025 high of 7.4% would confirm the cash trend, while falling below the -4.1% median would break it [D560][D561].
